examples.signature: Compare scalp EEG and an intracortical microelectrode array for the same motor-interface goal without declaring one universally superior
Trace an assistive motor BCI from neural activity through sensing, acquisition, decoding, device control, feedback, and user adaptation
Classify a cochlear implant as a sensory neuroprosthesis that encodes external sound into patterned stimulation rather than as a device that simply amplifies sound
Contrast open-loop stimulation with a closed-loop system that senses a biomarker and adapts therapy while preserving explicit safety constraints
Sort representative technologies into recording, modulation, restoration, rehabilitation, or augmentation goals while allowing one platform to serve more than one role
Classify a fingertip sensory pathway simultaneously by anatomical location (PNS/CNS), information direction (afferent), and functional organization (somatic sensory)
Map withdrawal from a hot surface through peripheral sensory input, spinal integration, somatic motor output, and ascending pathways to show that the spinal cord is not merely a relay cable
Compare cortex, spinal cord, peripheral nerve, and muscle as four possible interface locations for the same hand-movement restoration objective
Contrast somatic efferent control of wrist extension with autonomic efferent control of heart rate to separate efferent from voluntary
Map a cochlear implant from external sound through encoded stimulation, auditory nerve activity, brainstem and higher CNS pathways, perception, and behavioral adaptation

Trace one simplified motor neuron across soma-proximal, axonal, peripheral-nerve, and downstream-muscle observation sites to show that one pathway produces different measured signals at different biological levels
Use two ionic compartments separated by a potassium-selective membrane to build qualitative intuition for competing concentration and electrical forces
Contrast intracellular inside-versus-outside membrane-voltage measurement with extracellular field recording produced by transmembrane ionic currents
Compare similarly sized myelinated and unmyelinated axons to show why glial myelin changes propagation dynamics, recording timing, and stimulation recruitment

Trace one stored microvolt-scale digital sample backward through amplifier, electrode, electrode-tissue interface, extracellular field, transmembrane current, channel states, and metabolically maintained ion gradients
Use a potassium-selective membrane to trace the outward chemical tendency, inward electrical tendency, and their balance at the potassium equilibrium potential
Estimate illustrative potassium and sodium Nernst equilibrium potentials from intracellular/extracellular concentration ratios at body temperature
Double extracellular potassium in an illustrative neuron and show how the potassium equilibrium potential becomes less negative, shifting a K-dominated resting state
Use a simplified conductance-weighted membrane model to show why dominant potassium conductance places resting voltage much closer to E_K than to E_Na
Interpret a negative intracellular voltage reading as a local potential difference relative to an extracellular reference rather than an absolute voltage stored in the neuron
Trace one action potential through local depolarization, threshold crossing, Na-driven upstroke, Na-channel inactivation, delayed K conductance, repolarization, afterhyperpolarization, and recovery
Compare passive subthreshold voltage decay with regenerative axonal propagation driven by local current spread and repeated threshold crossing
Compare second stimuli arriving during absolute refractory, relative refractory, and recovered membrane states using channel availability rather than time labels alone
Compare unmyelinated continuous regeneration with myelinated internodal passive spread and node-of-Ranvier regeneration to explain saltatory conduction

Compare intracellular and extracellular recordings of the same action potential to show why extracellular spikes are geometry-dependent current-field signatures rather than scaled intracellular waveforms

Compare two receptor mechanisms for the same transmitter to show that postsynaptic excitation or inhibition depends on receptor, ionic selectivity, reversal potential, and membrane state rather than transmitter name alone

Trace one chemical synaptic event from presynaptic action-potential arrival through Ca2+ entry, vesicle fusion, transmitter release, receptor activation, conductance change, current, and postsynaptic potential
Compare slow versus rapid presynaptic firing at one excitatory synapse to show how overlapping graded postsynaptic potentials create temporal summation
Combine two excitatory synapses with one inhibitory conductance to show spatial integration, conductance interaction, and why inhibition is not fixed arithmetic subtraction

Model one chemical synapse as a dynamic signal-processing block mapping a presynaptic spike train through release probability, vesicle and receptor state, and postsynaptic membrane state to a synaptic-current or conductance waveform

Compare two behavioral conditions whose first recorded neuron has the same firing rate but whose full multi-neuron population activity vectors differ, showing why population patterns can disambiguate states that one unit cannot
Compare identical recurrent circuit connectivity under different excitability and adaptation states to show that connectivity plus current state plus input determines circuit response

Trace a reaching movement through visual estimation, movement planning, descending and spinal circuits, muscle activation, movement, and sensory feedback to show behavior as a closed sensorimotor loop

Compare single-unit, multi-unit, local-field, ECoG, and EEG measurements around the same finger movement to demonstrate that recording modalities sample different physical aggregates and neural scales
Interpret a high-accuracy movement decoder from fifty recorded neurons as predictive population information without incorrectly claiming those neurons uniquely cause the behavior
Represent one neuron's activity as raw extracellular voltage, detected spike times, and a smoothed firing-rate estimate to separate biological event, measured waveform, and derived feature

Compare the same synchronized cortical event as seen by intracortical field recording, ECoG, and scalp EEG to show how source geometry, volume conduction, referencing, and sensor location change the observed electrical signal
examples.domain: electrical signal scale and field mixing

examples.signature: Compare a rapid spike-rate change with an extracellular dopamine transient during the same task to distinguish electrical event measurements from neurochemical concentration-related measurements
Compare near-immediate electrophysiological changes with a delayed BOLD response following the same cortical activation to separate neural timing from hemodynamic measurement latency

Choose among single-unit electrophysiology, EEG, neurochemical sensing, and fMRI for four different scientific questions to make modality choice follow the target physical variable and required tradeoffs

Trace one extracellular action potential through transmembrane current, tissue conduction, electrode interface, amplification, filtering, digitization, spike detection, sorting, and firing-pattern inference
Show how a component above the Nyquist frequency can alias into a lower apparent rhythm when analog anti-alias filtering is insufficient before sampling
Follow a mixed extracellular recording through filtering, event detection, waveform alignment, feature extraction, and spike sorting to show that a putative unit is an inferred data object

Design backward from a 20-millisecond cursor-velocity decoder update requirement to derive constraints on neural features, windows, sampling, front-end range, electrode stability, and end-to-end latency
Separate amplifier calibration, spike-sort validation, and decoder generalization into three distinct validation layers so component accuracy is not confused with biological inference validity
